system:
You are the planning lead of a biomedical data-analysis agent. You receive one scientific question, the data provider's description of a dataset, a measured profile of the data, and a list of measured difficulties. Your job is to compile the question into a precise analysis objective that a team could execute and that an auditor could check.

Rules
- The question decides everything: what is estimated, which inputs are allowed, which are forbidden, and what must be compared with what. Do not optimise for the highest score; optimise for answering this question validly.
- Forbidden inputs must each come with the reason they would invalidate an answer to THIS question.
- Acceptance criteria must be checkable. For each one give: a short statement, the key of one deterministic check from the list provided, and the rule by which any threshold is derived from data. Never write a numeric threshold of your own; only a 5% false discovery rate and a 95% confidence level are fixed conventions.
- State the scope of the conclusion: to which units it applies and what it does not show.
- Use only facts given to you. Do not invent dataset properties.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these fields:
{
 "question": string (verbatim),
 "task_family": one of the family keys provided,
 "analysis_unit": string,
 "estimand": string (the quantity to be estimated, in one sentence),
 "target": string (what is predicted or compared),
 "allowed_inputs": [string],
 "forbidden_inputs": [string],
 "forbidden_reasons": {forbidden input: reason},
 "required_comparators": [string] (baselines / rulers every plan must be compared with),
 "primary_metric": string,
 "secondary_metrics": [string],
 "acceptance_criteria": [{"id": "A1", "statement": string, "check": check key, "rule": string}],
 "conclusion_options": [string] (the mutually exclusive answers the analysis may end with),
 "conclusion_scope": string,
 "notes": string
}
prompt:
SCIENTIFIC QUESTION:
Using the paired RNA and ATAC measurements, learn the cross-modal relationship. For cells of the same donor that took no part in training and for which only ATAC is provided, for which genes can the variation in RNA expression be predicted reliably?

DATASET DESCRIPTION (from the data provider):
name: 10x Genomics Multiome, PBMC from one healthy donor (granulocytes removed, about 10k cells)
unit: cell
description: 'Each development cell has two count vectors measured in the same nucleus: RNA (UMI counts per gene)
  and ATAC (fragment counts per accessibility peak). Held-out cells of the same donor provide ATAC only. A peak
  annotation links each peak to nearby genes with the distance to the transcription start site and a promoter/distal
  flag. Gene start coordinates are available.'
label_provenance:
  statement: The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities
    jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement.
  implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it
    cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
scope_of_inference: cells of the same donor that were not used for training; nothing about other donors
how_predictions_are_scored: 'The evaluator holds the RNA of the held-out cells. Each held-out cell''s RNA reads
  were split at random into two independent halves, A and B (binomial thinning). Every method is scored against
  half B after log-normalisation: for each gene, the Pearson correlation r between predicted and observed values
  across held-out cells. Genes in scope and the cluster number of the cell-type baseline were frozen from development
  cells only and are part of the view.'
rulers:
  ceiling: an RNA-to-RNA model that sees half A of the held-out cells and predicts half B; it marks what measurement
    noise allows
  floor_1_cell_type: cluster cells on ATAC, predict each cell by its cluster's mean expression (cluster number frozen
    from development cells)
  floor_2_gene_activity: sum of ATAC counts over the promoter and nearby peaks of the gene, no learning
  floor_3_depth: prediction from ATAC sequencing depth alone
  floor_4_simple_learners: ridge, k-nearest-neighbour and partial-least-squares regression on the ATAC latent space
decision_rule: '"Reliably predicted" means predicted beyond cell identity. Each in-scope gene is placed in one of
  three groups: (0) cannot be judged - the ceiling itself is not above the permutation null for this gene; (1) not
  beyond the cell-type baseline - the method''s r is not significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r; (2)
  predicts variation beyond cell type - the method''s r is significantly above the cluster-mean baseline''s r (paired
  bootstrap over cells, Benjamini-Hochberg across all in-scope genes, false discovery rate 5%). Thresholds come
  from the data by these rules; only the 5% false discovery rate and the 95% confidence level are conventions. An
  answer of "few or no genes are predicted beyond cell type" is acceptable if that is what the evidence shows.'
deliverable: A prediction matrix (held-out cells x in-scope genes, log-normalised scale), the list of genes the
  method claims to predict beyond cell type, and its own estimate of each gene's correlation with an interval.

MEASURED DATA PROFILE:
{
 "n_development_units": 7288,
 "n_held_out_units": 3124,
 "modalities": {
  "rna": {
   "features": 13536,
   "available_for": "development cells only",
   "fraction_zero": 0.8534380530643333,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 3830.0
  },
  "atac": {
   "features": 108377,
   "available_for": "all cells",
   "fraction_zero": 0.9281561742430454,
   "median_counts_per_cell": 20586.5
  }
 },
 "pairing": "both modalities measured in the same cell for every development cell",
 "genes_in_scope": 11282,
 "peak_gene_links": 87029,
 "cell_type_baseline_k": 20
}

MEASURED DIFFICULTIES (most severe first):
- D1 [measurement_noise, severity high] RNA counts are 85.3% zeros (median 3800 UMIs per cell). Splitting each cell's reads into two independent halves, a gene's value in one half correlates with the other half at a median r of 0.111 across 11282 in-scope genes (90th percentile 0.306). Implication: Per-gene correlation with a single noisy reading is bounded well below 1; scores must be read against a noise ceiling, and validating against smoothed or full-depth targets overstates accuracy.
- D2 [class_imbalance, severity high] The provided annotation has 19 cell types in the development set, from 1936 cells (CD14 Mono) down to 15 (Plasma). Implication: Rare populations contribute little to a pooled correlation and are easy to underfit; within-cluster correlation should be reported alongside the pooled one.
- D3 [multiple_comparisons, severity high] 11282 genes are in scope and each gets its own test. Implication: Gene-level claims need false-discovery-rate control across all in-scope genes.
- D4 [label_provenance, severity high] The cell-type annotation supplied with the development cells was produced by clustering both modalities jointly (weighted nearest neighbours) and curating the clusters by hand. It is not an independent measurement. Implication: The annotation may describe the data but must not be used as a model input for held-out cells (it cannot be known without their RNA) and must not serve as evaluation truth.
- D5 [technical_confounding, severity medium] ATAC depth and RNA depth are correlated across cells (r = 0.36 on the log scale). A model that sees only ATAC depth reaches a mean per-gene r of 0.032. Implication: Report a depth-only baseline; a predictor must beat it before its signal is called biological.
- D6 [strong_baseline, severity medium] Predicting each cell by the mean expression of its ATAC cluster (k = 20, chosen by cross-validation inside the development set) gives a mean per-gene r of 0.130; ridge regression on the ATAC latent space gives 0.143; the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling is 0.194. Implication: Most predictable variation is cell identity. A plan answers the question only through what it predicts beyond the cluster-mean baseline, gene by gene, on the same cells.
- D7 [statistical_power, severity low] With thousands of cells a correlation as small as 0.037 already exceeds 95% of the permutation null (3124 held-out cells will be scored). Implication: Significance against zero is nearly automatic and cannot be the headline; effect size and the comparison with the cell-type baseline carry the conclusion.

TASK FAMILIES (choose one key):
- cross_modal_prediction: Predict one measured modality from another, feature by feature, for units that provide only the source modality.
- incremental_value_classification: Estimate how much a second modality adds to a baseline modality for predicting a class label.
- single_modality_classification: Estimate how well one modality alone predicts a class label.
- cross_modal_retrieval: Match each unit's profile in one modality to its own profile in another modality among many candidates.

DETERMINISTIC CHECKS AVAILABLE TO THE AUDIT (use these keys in acceptance_criteria.check):
- no_forbidden_inputs: the plan uses no input the objective forbids
- correct_split_unit: the plan's own validation keeps each analysis unit (and everything nested in it) on one side of every split
- beats_required_floors: the method's primary metric is above each required floor / comparator on the same units
- beats_simple_reference: the method is compared directly with the simplest valid plan on the same units
- training_converged: training curves exist and the last part of the curve is no longer improving
- scored_on_unsmoothed_truth: scores are computed against measured, unsmoothed values of units not used for fitting
- both_arms_same_units: the comparison arms use the same units and the same missing-value handling
- selection_nested: model or configuration choices were made without the units the reported score is computed on
- interval_reported: the primary estimate comes with a confidence interval at the 95% level
- multiplicity_controlled: claims about many features control the false discovery rate at 5%
- within_budget: the full run fits the declared budget
- deliverable_complete: the required deliverable exists, has the right shape and contains only finite values

 ],

 },
 "required_comparators": [
  "ceiling: RNA-to-RNA model trained on development splits to predict log-normalised half B from independent half A and evaluated on unseen cells' half A to predict half B (marks the upper bound permitted by RNA measurement noise)",
  "permutation_null: per-gene cell-permutation null distribution of Pearson correlation r used to determine whether the RNA-to-RNA ceiling itself is detectable above chance (Group 0 screening)",
  "floor_1_cell_type: ATAC cluster-mean expression baseline (clustering cells on ATAC alone with frozen k = 20 fitted on training cells and predicting each unseen cell by its assigned cluster's training mean log-normalised expression)",
  "floor_2_gene_activity: unlearned gene-activity score summing ATAC fragment counts across promoter and linked nearby peaks per gene",
  "floor_3_depth: technical confounding baseline predicting log-normalised RNA expression from ATAC sequencing depth alone",
  "floor_4_simple_learners: ridge regression, k-nearest-neighbour regression, and partial-least-squares regression fitted on the ATAC latent space"
 ],
 "primary_metric": "Per-gene out-of-sample Pearson correlation r between ATAC-predicted log-normalised RNA and observed log-normalised binomial-thinned (half B) RNA across unseen cells, paired with per-gene excess correlation over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline (delta_r = r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type) tested via paired cell bootstrap with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control at 5% across all 11,282 in-scope genes.",
 "secondary_metrics": [
  "Counts and proportions of the 11,282 in-scope genes assigned to Group 0 (ceiling not above permutation null), Group 1 (not significantly above floor_1_cell_type at 5% FDR), and Group 2 (significantly above floor_1_cell_type at 5% FDR)",
  "Mean, median, interquartile range, and 90th percentile of per-gene Pearson correlation r and delta_r across all 11,282 in-scope genes and across judgeable genes (Groups 1 and 2)",
  "Noise-normalised predictive performance per gene (fraction of the RNA-to-RNA ceiling achieved, r_method / r_ceiling, and fraction of post-cell-type headroom captured, (r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type) / (r_ceiling - r_floor_1_cell_type), for judgeable genes)",
  "Within-cluster per-gene Pearson correlation r computed inside ATAC-defined clusters (k = 20) and, on development validation splits, inside the 19 curated cell-type populations to diagnose underfitting on rare populations versus abundant ones",
  "Per-gene and mean correlation gains over the technical ATAC depth baseline (r_method - r_floor_3_depth) and unlearned gene-activity baseline (r_method - r_floor_2_gene_activity)"
 ],
 "acceptance_criteria": [
  {
   "id": "A1",
   "statement": "All preprocessing, feature engineering, baseline construction, model training, selection, and inference steps exclude every declared forbidden input.",
   "check": "no_forbidden_inputs",
   "rule": "Audit of data lineage confirms zero access to held-out RNA, zero access to held-out ATAC prior to final frozen inference, zero use of curated WNN annotations as features/targets/truth, zero target smoothing/full-depth substitution in validation scoring, and zero external datasets."
  },
  {
   "id": "A2",
   "statement": "Internal validation splits development data strictly at the cell level so each cell and all derived counts, binomial-thinned halves, latent embeddings, scalers, and ATAC clusters remain entirely on one side of every split.",
   "check": "correct_split_unit",

  },
  {
   "id": "A3",

  },
  {
   "id": "A4",
   "statement": "All internal validation scores for the method, floors, and ceiling are computed against log-normalised observed RNA from an independent binomial-thinned read half (half B) of unseen cells without smoothing, imputation, or full-depth target substitution.",
   "check": "scored_on_unsmoothed_truth",
   "rule": "Validation ground truth for every unseen development cell is produced by independent equal-probability binomial thinning of its raw observed UMI counts into halves A and B followed by standard log-normalisation of half B, with no denoising or cross-cell smoothing."
  },
  {
   "id": "A5",
   "statement": "The candidate predictor, ceiling, and all four floor baselines are evaluated on the exact same out-of-sample cell order, identical half-B target values, and identical set of frozen in-scope genes.",
   "check": "both_arms_same_units",
   "rule": "Every comparison arm is scored over the identical evaluation cell indices and identical frozen in-scope gene list using uniform constant-vector handling (zero correlation assigned when prediction or target variance is zero, with no unit or gene dropping)."
  },
  {
   "id": "A6",
   "statement": "Before attributing cross-modal predictions to biological chromatin-expression coupling, the selected predictor must outperform both the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline and the unlearned gene-activity baseline in aggregate across in-scope genes on the same unseen cells.",
   "check": "beats_required_floors",
   "rule": "Mean per-gene Pearson correlation across all frozen in-scope genes for the selected method exceeds the data-derived mean per-gene correlation of floor_3_depth and floor_2_gene_activity on the same validation cells, with the paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval for each mean difference lying strictly above zero."
  },
  {
   "id": "A7",
   "statement": "Any proposed cross-modal model is benchmarked directly on identical splits against simple ATAC latent-space learners (ridge, k-nearest-neighbour, and partial-least-squares regression) and only supersedes them if justified by inner-validation performance.",
   "check": "beats_simple_reference",
   "rule": "Paired comparison on identical unseen cells against floor_4_simple_learners; a more complex model is selected over the strongest simple learner only if its inner-cross-validation mean per-gene Pearson correlation exceeds that of the strongest simple learner."
  },
  {
   "id": "A8",
   "statement": "Any iterative or gradient-trained cross-modal or ceiling model logs training and inner-validation curves demonstrating convergence without divergence.",
   "check": "training_converged",
   "rule": "Logged inner-validation loss or correlation curves plateau prior to stopping (early-stopping criterion satisfied or final optimization segment shows non-improving validation objective), and analytical/linear solvers complete with finite converged solutions."
  },
  {
   "id": "A9",
   "statement": "Gene-level claims of reliable prediction beyond cell type control multiplicity across all frozen in-scope genes at a 5% false discovery rate via paired cell bootstrap after screening genes against the RNA-to-RNA ceiling permutation null.",
   "check": "multiplicity_controlled",
   "rule": "Genes whose RNA-to-RNA ceiling correlation does not exceed the 95% level of the data-derived cell-permutation null are placed in Group 0; across all in-scope genes, paired cell-bootstrap p-values testing r_method > r_floor_1_cell_type are adjusted via Benjamini-Hochberg at a 5% false discovery rate, placing judgeable genes passing the 5% false discovery rate threshold into Group 2 and remaining judgeable genes into Group 1."
  },
  {
   "id": "A10",
   "statement": "Every in-scope gene's estimated out-of-sample Pearson correlation r and paired gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline, as well as aggregate cross-gene summaries, include two-sided 95% confidence intervals.",
   "check": "interval_reported",
   "rule": "Nonparametric bootstrap resampling over unseen evaluation cells provides 95% confidence intervals for per-gene r, per-gene delta_r (r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type), and aggregate mean/median correlation metrics."
  },
  {
   "id": "A11",
   "statement": "The final deliverable contains a complete, finite log-normalised prediction matrix for all held-out cells across all frozen in-scope genes (matching data profile dimensions), the explicit list of Group 2 genes claimed beyond cell type alongside Group 0/1/2 classifications, and per-gene correlation estimates with 95% confidence intervals.",
   "check": "deliverable_complete",
   "rule": "Held-out prediction array has exact shape n_held_out_units by genes_in_scope from the measured data profile with strictly finite numeric entries, paired with a complete gene-level table covering every frozen in-scope gene with finite correlation estimates, 95% confidence bounds, and group assignments."
  },
  {
   "id": "A12",
   "statement": "The entire workflow including preprocessing, nested cross-validation, baseline and ceiling estimation, cell-bootstrap hypothesis testing, and held-out inference finishes within declared compute limits.",
   "check": "within_budget",
   "rule": "Total wall-clock execution time and peak memory footprint remain within the declared computational budget of the run environment."
  }
 ],
 "conclusion_options": [
  "No biological cross-modal signal beyond technical confounding: ATAC-to-RNA predictors fail to exceed the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline (floor_3_depth) or unlearned gene-activity baseline (floor_2_gene_activity) on unseen cells, so reliable RNA prediction cannot be claimed for any gene.",
  "Predictable RNA variation is wholly explained by coarse cell identity (no genes reliably predicted beyond cell type): ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical depth and unlearned floors, but zero in-scope genes show statistically significant correlation above the ATAC cluster-mean baseline (floor_1_cell_type, k = 20) at a 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (all judgeable genes fall in Group 1, with noisy unjudgeable genes in Group 0).",
  "A specific subset of genes is reliably predicted beyond cell identity: ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical floors and an enumerated proper subset of judgeable in-scope genes (Group 2 at 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate via paired cell bootstrap) exhibits statistically reliable expression variation predicted from ATAC beyond the k = 20 ATAC cluster-mean baseline, whereas remaining judgeable genes reflect cell identity alone (Group 1) and remaining genes lie below the single-cell RNA noise ceiling (Group 0).",
  "All judgeable genes are reliably predicted beyond cell identity: ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical floors and every in-scope gene whose RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling exceeds the 95% permutation null achieves statistically significant correlation above the k = 20 ATAC cluster-mean baseline at a 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate."
 ],
 "conclusion_scope": "Conclusions apply strictly to unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells (single nuclei) from the same healthy donor assayed under the same 10x Genomics Multiome protocol and sequencing-depth regime across the 11,282 frozen in-scope genes, scored against noisy binomial-thinned single-cell RNA counts. The analysis shows nothing about generalisation to other donors, disease states, granulocytes, other tissues, or different assay protocols; it does not establish causal cis- or trans-regulatory mechanisms between chromatin peaks and transcription; for Group 0 genes, it reflects measurement-noise limits (85.3% RNA zeros) rather than biological independence; pooled across-cell correlations are weighted toward abundant PBMC populations (such as CD14 Monocytes) and do not prove reliable intra-population prediction within rare cell types (such as Plasma cells) unless corroborated by within-cluster correlation diagnostics; and it does not validate curated WNN cell-type labels as ground truth.",
 "notes": "1) Evaluator held-out RNA is unavailable during execution, so the deliverable's per-gene correlation estimates, 95% confidence intervals, and Group 0/1/2 gene classifications must be derived from outer folds of nested cross-validation on the 7,288 development cells using independent binomial thinning (splitting raw UMI counts with probability 0.5 into half A and half B prior to log-normalisation) to faithfully replicate held-out scoring; Note that predictions output for the 3,124 held-out cells must match the log-normalised half-B scale, so models trained on full development UMI counts should either train on or calibrate to the binomial-thinned half-B log-normalised target distribution. 2) Distinguish raw split-half correlation (median r = 0.111 in D1) from the learned multi-gene RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling model (mean r = 0.194 in D6), fitting the half-A-to-half-B ceiling model strictly on training cells and evaluating on unseen validation cells. 3) Construct floor_1_cell_type using ATAC features only with frozen k = 20 fitted on training cells (never using curated WNN labels). 4) Because N = 3,124 (and thousands of out-of-fold development cells) makes tiny correlations (~0.037) significant against zero (D7), never base reliability claims on p-values against zero; rely strictly on paired bootstrap delta_r over floor_1_cell_type at 5% BH FDR alongside effect sizes relative to the RNA-to-RNA ceiling. 5) Report within-ATAC-cluster (k = 20) correlations and, on development validation folds only, descriptive within-WNN-type correlations across the 19 imbalanced populations (1,936 down to 15 cells, D2) to diagnose whether Group 2 gains reflect genuine within-cell-type state variation or finer subclustering among abundant lineages."
}

json.estimand: For each of the 11,282 frozen in-scope genes, the out-of-sample Pearson correlation r between ATAC-predicted log-normalised RNA expression and observed log-normalised RNA expression from an independent binomial-thinned read half (half B) across unseen cells of the same donor, together with the paired correlation gain over an ATAC-only cluster-mean baseline (k = 20) that determines whether variation beyond cell identity is reliably predicted.
json.target: Log-normalised RNA expression across the 11,282 frozen in-scope genes for unseen cells (scored against unsmoothed binomial-thinned half-B observed UMI counts) and the resulting per-gene classification into Group 0 (unjudgeable below noise ceiling), Group 1 (not beyond ATAC cell-type baseline), or Group 2 (reliably predicted beyond ATAC cell-type baseline at 5% FDR).
allowed_inputs: Development cells' paired ATAC fragment count matrix (7,288 cells x 108,377 peaks) and RNA UMI count matrix (7,288 cells x 13,536 genes) for model training, baseline fitting, and nested internal cross-validation

Independent binomial-thinned RNA count splits (halves A and B) generated within development cells to mirror half-B evaluation targets and fit the RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling without leaking across cell splits

Held-out cells' ATAC fragment count matrix (3,124 cells x 108,377 peaks) strictly at inference time after all training, clustering, representation learning, and model selection on development cells are frozen
Provided peak-to-gene annotation table (87,029 peak-gene links with distance to transcription start site and promoter/distal flag) and gene start coordinates
Frozen list of 11,282 in-scope genes and frozen ATAC cluster number (k = 20) derived from development cells

Development cells' curated 19-type joint-modality (WNN) annotation strictly for exploratory data profiling and stratified post-hoc diagnostic reporting on development validation folds (never as model input or ground-truth target)
forbidden_inputs: Held-out cells' ATAC measurements during training, representation learning, clustering, normalisation, or hyperparameter selection
Curated joint-modality (WNN) cell-type annotations as a model input feature, training target/auxiliary loss, or evaluation truth
Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinned full-depth RNA expression as the validation scoring target
External multiome datasets, external expression atlases, or pretrained cross-modal weights

forbidden_reasons.Held-out cells' RNA measurements: Held-out RNA is withheld to evaluate cross-modal prediction for ATAC-only cells; accessing any part of held-out RNA directly leaks the target modality and invalidates out-of-sample inference.
forbidden_reasons.Held-out cells' ATAC measurements during: The scientific question explicitly asks about cells of the same donor that took no part in training; transductive use of held-out ATAC in latent-space learning, clustering, or tuning violates this out-of-sample condition.
forbidden_reasons.Curated joint-modality (WNN) cell-type a: These annotations were produced by weighted-nearest-neighbour clustering of both RNA and ATAC jointly followed by manual curation; they cannot be known for ATAC-only cells without their RNA and are not an independent ground-truth measurement.
forbidden_reasons.Smoothed, imputed, denoised, or unthinne: Observed RNA is 85.3% zeros and evaluator scoring uses log-normalised binomial-thinned half-B counts; validating against smoothed, imputed, or full-depth RNA artificially suppresses measurement noise and overstates predictable correlation relative to the true noise ceiling.
forbidden_reasons.External multiome datasets, external exp: The question requires learning the cross-modal relationship from the paired RNA and ATAC measurements in this dataset; external biological references or pretrained weights would confound what can be learned from the provided paired measurements.

required_comparators: ceiling: RNA-to-RNA model trained on development splits to predict log-normalised half B from independent half A and evaluated on unseen cells' half A to predict half B (marks the upper bound permitted by RNA measurement noise)
permutation_null: per-gene cell-permutation null distribution of Pearson correlation r used to determine whether the RNA-to-RNA ceiling itself is detectable above chance (Group 0 screening)

floor_1_cell_type: ATAC cluster-mean expression baseline (clustering cells on ATAC alone with frozen k = 20 fitted on training cells and predicting each unseen cell by its assigned cluster's training mean log-normalised expression)
floor_2_gene_activity: unlearned gene-activity score summing ATAC fragment counts across promoter and linked nearby peaks per gene
floor_3_depth: technical confounding baseline predicting log-normalised RNA expression from ATAC sequencing depth alone
floor_4_simple_learners: ridge regression, k-nearest-neighbour regression, and partial-least-squares regression fitted on the ATAC latent space
json.primary_metric: Per-gene out-of-sample Pearson correlation r between ATAC-predicted log-normalised RNA and observed log-normalised binomial-thinned (half B) RNA across unseen cells, paired with per-gene excess correlation over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline (delta_r = r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type) tested via paired cell bootstrap with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate control at 5% across all 11,282 in-scope genes.
secondary_metrics: Counts and proportions of the 11,282 in-scope genes assigned to Group 0 (ceiling not above permutation null), Group 1 (not significantly above floor_1_cell_type at 5% FDR), and Group 2 (significantly above floor_1_cell_type at 5% FDR)
Mean, median, interquartile range, and 90th percentile of per-gene Pearson correlation r and delta_r across all 11,282 in-scope genes and across judgeable genes (Groups 1 and 2)

Noise-normalised predictive performance per gene (fraction of the RNA-to-RNA ceiling achieved, r_method / r_ceiling, and fraction of post-cell-type headroom captured, (r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type) / (r_ceiling - r_floor_1_cell_type), for judgeable genes)

Within-cluster per-gene Pearson correlation r computed inside ATAC-defined clusters (k = 20) and, on development validation splits, inside the 19 curated cell-type populations to diagnose underfitting on rare populations versus abundant ones
Per-gene and mean correlation gains over the technical ATAC depth baseline (r_method - r_floor_3_depth) and unlearned gene-activity baseline (r_method - r_floor_2_gene_activity)

acceptance_criteria.statement: All preprocessing, feature engineering, baseline construction, model training, selection, and inference steps exclude every declared forbidden input.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Audit of data lineage confirms zero access to held-out RNA, zero access to held-out ATAC prior to final frozen inference, zero use of curated WNN annotations as features/targets/truth, zero target smoothing/full-depth substitution in validation scoring, and zero external datasets.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Internal validation splits development data strictly at the cell level so each cell and all derived counts, binomial-thinned halves, latent embeddings, scalers, and ATAC clusters remain entirely on one side of every split.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Cell index sets for training and validation partitions are mutually disjoint in every fold, and all unsupervised or supervised parameters (peak filtering, TF-IDF/LSI/PCA projections, k = 20 ATAC clustering, scalers, and regression/model weights) are fitted exclusively on training-fold cells.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Model architectures, feature representations, loss weightings, and regularisation hyperparameters are chosen strictly within inner training/tuning splits without using the outer validation folds on which final correlation estimates and intervals are reported.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Outer-fold validation predictions used for estimating per-gene correlations, 95% confidence intervals, and Group 0/1/2 gene calls come exclusively from models whose configurations were selected using inner-loop development partitions only.

acceptance_criteria.statement: All internal validation scores for the method, floors, and ceiling are computed against log-normalised observed RNA from an independent binomial-thinned read half (half B) of unseen cells without smoothing, imputation, or full-depth target substitution.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Validation ground truth for every unseen development cell is produced by independent equal-probability binomial thinning of its raw observed UMI counts into halves A and B followed by standard log-normalisation of half B, with no denoising or cross-cell smoothing.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The candidate predictor, ceiling, and all four floor baselines are evaluated on the exact same out-of-sample cell order, identical half-B target values, and identical set of frozen in-scope genes.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Every comparison arm is scored over the identical evaluation cell indices and identical frozen in-scope gene list using uniform constant-vector handling (zero correlation assigned when prediction or target variance is zero, with no unit or gene dropping).

acceptance_criteria.statement: Before attributing cross-modal predictions to biological chromatin-expression coupling, the selected predictor must outperform both the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline and the unlearned gene-activity baseline in aggregate across in-scope genes on the same unseen cells.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Mean per-gene Pearson correlation across all frozen in-scope genes for the selected method exceeds the data-derived mean per-gene correlation of floor_3_depth and floor_2_gene_activity on the same validation cells, with the paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval for each mean difference lying strictly above zero.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Any proposed cross-modal model is benchmarked directly on identical splits against simple ATAC latent-space learners (ridge, k-nearest-neighbour, and partial-least-squares regression) and only supersedes them if justified by inner-validation performance.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Paired comparison on identical unseen cells against floor_4_simple_learners; a more complex model is selected over the strongest simple learner only if its inner-cross-validation mean per-gene Pearson correlation exceeds that of the strongest simple learner.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Any iterative or gradient-trained cross-modal or ceiling model logs training and inner-validation curves demonstrating convergence without divergence.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Logged inner-validation loss or correlation curves plateau prior to stopping (early-stopping criterion satisfied or final optimization segment shows non-improving validation objective), and analytical/linear solvers complete with finite converged solutions.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Gene-level claims of reliable prediction beyond cell type control multiplicity across all frozen in-scope genes at a 5% false discovery rate via paired cell bootstrap after screening genes against the RNA-to-RNA ceiling permutation null.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Genes whose RNA-to-RNA ceiling correlation does not exceed the 95% level of the data-derived cell-permutation null are placed in Group 0; across all in-scope genes, paired cell-bootstrap p-values testing r_method > r_floor_1_cell_type are adjusted via Benjamini-Hochberg at a 5% false discovery rate, placing judgeable genes passing the 5% false discovery rate threshold into Group 2 and remaining judgeable genes into Group 1.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Every in-scope gene's estimated out-of-sample Pearson correlation r and paired gain over the ATAC cluster-mean baseline, as well as aggregate cross-gene summaries, include two-sided 95% confidence intervals.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Nonparametric bootstrap resampling over unseen evaluation cells provides 95% confidence intervals for per-gene r, per-gene delta_r (r_method - r_floor_1_cell_type), and aggregate mean/median correlation metrics.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The final deliverable contains a complete, finite log-normalised prediction matrix for all held-out cells across all frozen in-scope genes (matching data profile dimensions), the explicit list of Group 2 genes claimed beyond cell type alongside Group 0/1/2 classifications, and per-gene correlation estimates with 95% confidence intervals.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Held-out prediction array has exact shape n_held_out_units by genes_in_scope from the measured data profile with strictly finite numeric entries, paired with a complete gene-level table covering every frozen in-scope gene with finite correlation estimates, 95% confidence bounds, and group assignments.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The entire workflow including preprocessing, nested cross-validation, baseline and ceiling estimation, cell-bootstrap hypothesis testing, and held-out inference finishes within declared compute limits.
acceptance_criteria.rule: Total wall-clock execution time and peak memory footprint remain within the declared computational budget of the run environment.

conclusion_options: No biological cross-modal signal beyond technical confounding: ATAC-to-RNA predictors fail to exceed the ATAC sequencing-depth baseline (floor_3_depth) or unlearned gene-activity baseline (floor_2_gene_activity) on unseen cells, so reliable RNA prediction cannot be claimed for any gene.

Predictable RNA variation is wholly explained by coarse cell identity (no genes reliably predicted beyond cell type): ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical depth and unlearned floors, but zero in-scope genes show statistically significant correlation above the ATAC cluster-mean baseline (floor_1_cell_type, k = 20) at a 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (all judgeable genes fall in Group 1, with noisy unjudgeable genes in Group 0).

A specific subset of genes is reliably predicted beyond cell identity: ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical floors and an enumerated proper subset of judgeable in-scope genes (Group 2 at 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate via paired cell bootstrap) exhibits statistically reliable expression variation predicted from ATAC beyond the k = 20 ATAC cluster-mean baseline, whereas remaining judgeable genes reflect cell identity alone (Group 1) and remaining genes lie below the single-cell RNA noise ceiling (Group 0).

All judgeable genes are reliably predicted beyond cell identity: ATAC-to-RNA prediction exceeds technical floors and every in-scope gene whose RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling exceeds the 95% permutation null achieves statistically significant correlation above the k = 20 ATAC cluster-mean baseline at a 5% Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate.
json.conclusion_scope: Conclusions apply strictly to unseen granulocyte-depleted peripheral blood mononuclear cells (single nuclei) from the same healthy donor assayed under the same 10x Genomics Multiome protocol and sequencing-depth regime across the 11,282 frozen in-scope genes, scored against noisy binomial-thinned single-cell RNA counts. The analysis shows nothing about generalisation to other donors, disease states, granulocytes, other tissues, or different assay protocols; it does not establish causal cis- or trans-regulatory mechanisms between chromatin peaks and transcription; for Group 0 genes, it reflects measurement-noise limits (85.3% RNA zeros) rather than biological independence; pooled across-cell correlations are weighted toward abundant PBMC populations (such as CD14 Monocytes) and do not prove reliable intra-population prediction within rare cell types (such as Plasma cells) unless corroborated by within-cluster correlation diagnostics; and it does not validate curated WNN cell-type labels as ground truth.
json.notes: 1) Evaluator held-out RNA is unavailable during execution, so the deliverable's per-gene correlation estimates, 95% confidence intervals, and Group 0/1/2 gene classifications must be derived from outer folds of nested cross-validation on the 7,288 development cells using independent binomial thinning (splitting raw UMI counts with probability 0.5 into half A and half B prior to log-normalisation) to faithfully replicate held-out scoring; Note that predictions output for the 3,124 held-out cells must match the log-normalised half-B scale, so models trained on full development UMI counts should either train on or calibrate to the binomial-thinned half-B log-normalised target distribution. 2) Distinguish raw split-half correlation (median r = 0.111 in D1) from the learned multi-gene RNA-to-RNA noise ceiling model (mean r = 0.194 in D6), fitting the half-A-to-half-B ceiling model strictly on training cells and evaluating on unseen validation cells. 3) Construct floor_1_cell_type using ATAC features only with frozen k = 20 fitted on training cells (never using curated WNN labels). 4) Because N = 3,124 (and thousands of out-of-fold development cells) makes tiny correlations (~0.037) significant against zero (D7), never base reliability claims on p-values against zero; rely strictly on paired bootstrap delta_r over floor_1_cell_type at 5% BH FDR alongside effect sizes relative to the RNA-to-RNA ceiling. 5) Report within-ATAC-cluster (k = 20) correlations and, on development validation folds only, descriptive within-WNN-type correlations across the 19 imbalanced populations (1,936 down to 15 cells, D2) to diagnose whether Group 2 gains reflect genuine within-cell-type state variation or finer subclustering among abundant lineages.
